thread.title: Marquette's Brian Hoener looks back on 15-6 season and facing 'those three' - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Marquette's Brian Hoener looks back on 15-6 season and facing 'those three' - NewsBreak

author: Pete Hayes
title: Marquette's Brian Hoener looks back on 15-6 season and facing 'those three' - NewsBreak
text:
By Pete Hayes ,
12 hours ago
Marquette's Parker Belchik controls the ball against Alton at Piasa Motor Fuels Field. (Pete Hayes/The Telegraph)
ALTON - Being ranked No. 4 in the state is a good gig. But if the No. 1, No. 2 and No. 3 teams are ahead of you and in your same area, it can be challenging.
Just ask Marquette soccer coach Brian Hoener.
Hoener, whose Explorers were beaten last week in the IHSA Wesclin 1A Regional championship game, was in that situation all season.
It was indeed a challenge.
Marquette finished the season 15-6, and all six of their losses were to three teams - all of which were ranked ahead of them in the weekly MaxPeps 1A state rankings heading into the title showdown.
"We won 15 games against a difficult schedule," Hoener said, as he reflected on the season. "But we didn't find a way to beat those three. It was a tough hurdle to get over for us."
"Those three" were Father McGivney, Belleville Althoff and Columbia.
The Explorers lost three times to top-ranked McGivney, twice to second-ranked Althoff and once to defending champ and third-ranked Columbia. In this week's rankings, with Marquette out of the playoffs, the Explorers have dropped to No. 5 behind Cristo Rey St. Martin, which is still alive and playing for a sectional championship.
"In three of those games, we had the lead - twice against Althoff," Hoener said. "We needed to find a way to make the plays at the right times to hold onto the lead.
"We're out of the playoffs now, but it would be hard to say we still aren't one of the top five to 10 teams in the state."
McGivney and Marquette were assigned to the Wesclin Regional, Columbia was sent to Murphysboro and Althoff had its own regional tournament. All three of those regions fed into the Columbia 1A Sectional. McGivney defeated Columbia 1-0 earlier this week in a semifinal, while Althoff defeated Waterloo Gibault 5-0 in the other semi.
"I would be surprised if the McGivney-Althoff winner doesn't go on to win the state championship," Hoener said.
When Marquette was assigned to the same regional, Hoener was not surprised.
"We knew where the road would eventually go through," he said, "especially having to face one of them so early."
In the regional final against McGivney, Marquette held an early lead before the Griffins rallied for a 4-1 win.
Aside from six losses to three schools, Marquette won 16 times.
"I was very happy with the way we played," Hoener said. "We beat teams like Alton (twice), Jacksonville and Orchard Farms."
Marquette started its season by winning the Alton High Tournament.
"That was a great way for us to get in some early games," Hoener said, "and we got solid results against some good teams."
Marquette had a go-to scorer this season, even though Hoener was wondering where his team's goals would come from until Parker Belchik stepped onto the field.
Belchik, a senior, elected to play for Marquette this season after playing previously for Lou Fusz MLS Next. The MLS Next season runs from September through July, directly overlapping with high school sports seasons and causing scheduling conflicts for matches and major national showcase events. Also, IHSA regulations prohibit players from dual-rostering during a season.
Belchik wanted to play his senior season with his friends at MCHS - and they're glad he did.
Belchik scored 33 goals and added 11 assists. Hoener said his coaching approach didn't change because of Belchik.
"Not at all," Hoener said. "He fit right in with what we do. He plays at such a high level; he adapts as needed."
Belchik, who's considered one of the top defenders in his age group in MLS Next, was moved up to forward by Hoener.
"We needed him to score goals for us," Hoener said, "and he obviously did that."
Belchik's work ethic was mirrored by his teammates.
"We had a pretty young team," Hoener said, "and they matured and improved every game - you could see it. I had some questions about where our scoring would come from until Parker got here."
Another Parker - sophomore Parker Hough - was the second-leading scorer for Marquette with 10 goals and 13 assists.
"Parker Hough played everywhere for us," Hoener said, "and he was effective everywhere. He was our 'Swiss Army Knife.'"
The Explorers’ defense, including sophomore goalie Chase Kopp, logged 10 shutouts, including one streak of three straight clean sheets.
"Parker Hough, William Waters, Zach Bober, Logan Anderson, James Fischer, Eli Baggio - they had solid seasons, Hoener said. "And you could see Chase Kopp improving game by game. He made some special saves. He started for us as a freshman and had a good sophomore year. Chase has two more years, and that makes the prospect for the next two years exciting."
Closing out games was a challenge, Hoener said.
"There were moments in those games we were the better team - maybe 40 to 50 minutes," he said. "But there were also times we weren't, for 20 or 30 minutes.
"We'll be working on being the better team for 80 minutes."
